label: CodeBuddy Code
description: One conversation with CodeBuddy Code, Tencent's coding agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, CodeBuddy Code runs on your machine (a local install only) from your own install of `codebuddy` with your own login, working in `folder`. If `codebuddy` is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own, shared by the whole machine, before the node runs. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. Refusing one of its permission requests ends its whole turn. Your program's tools reach the model under their own names, and one named like a CodeBuddy Code tool takes that tool's place. That rests on settings CodeBuddy Code does not document: one that stops reading them fails the turn, saying so and which version to install. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission mode, the model and the effort, instructions added to its system prompt, extra folders and which CodeBuddy site the account belongs to.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run CodeBuddy Code in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A CodeBuddyCodeAccess's `access`: a CodeBuddy API key. Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, CodeBuddy Code uses the login already on it.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder CodeBuddy Code works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the CodeBuddy Code program to run, when it is not the `codebuddy` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What CodeBuddy Code may do without asking. `ask`: every request it would put to a person comes out of AskAgent as a question. `accept_edits`: file edits go ahead, the rest asks. `auto`: its own classifier lets safe actions through and asks about the rest. `plan`: it only plans, and asks before acting on the plan. `dont_ask`: anything it would ask about is refused without asking. `bypass`: nothing asks, not even before a command it rates dangerous (`rm -rf`); for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: The model to use, by its id. Left out, CodeBuddy Code's own default.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Effort
inputs.description: How hard the model thinks, for a model that reasons. Left out, the model's default.

inputs.name: appendSystemPrompt
inputs.label: Add to the system prompt
inputs.description: Instructions added to its system prompt, for every turn.

inputs.name: addDirs
inputs.label: Extra folders
inputs.description: Folders besides `folder` CodeBuddy Code may read and change.

inputs.name: edition
inputs.label: CodeBuddy site
inputs.description: Which CodeBuddy site the account belongs to: `public` (codebuddy.ai) or `internal` (China, copilot.tencent.com). Left out, `public`.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: CodeBuddyCode '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
CodeBuddyCode '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a CodeBuddyCodeAccess on `access`.
CodeBuddyCode '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
CodeBuddyCode '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, accept_edits, auto, plan, dont_ask, bypass.
CodeBuddyCode '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
CodeBuddyCode '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs CodeBuddy Code itself.
